requirements.text: Freeze each execution phase to an exact repository and SharedInfo commit, record drift, and stop when the reviewed assumptions are invalid.
Preserve existing Simple Chat HTTP routes, JSON and SSE contracts, authorization scopes, error semantics, idempotency, and concurrency behavior.
Preserve Simple Chat definition, conversation, streaming, cancellation, recovery, main-page, and floating-shell behavior.
Preserve existing Agent catalog, settings, main chat, floating chat, Process chat, Project Structure context, and execution behavior.
Preparation produces documentation and validators only; implementation starts only through SB01 execution.

Reuse AgentFramework.Llm.Abstractions, AgentFramework.Llm.Conversations, AgentFramework.Llm.ProviderRuntime, Conversations.Components, and Conversations.Shell instead of duplicating generic chat foundations.
Move the Simple Chat feature family from Modules.LlmChats namespaces and paths into role-qualified CanDoItAll.AgentFramework.Llm.SimpleChats projects under src/MAF/SimpleChats.
Use exactly five Simple Chat libraries—Core, Application, Runtime, Persistence, and Components—unless CP0 records evidence and an approved replacement map.

Core owns typed identifiers, aggregates, operation state/events/transitions, validation, and fingerprints; Application owns use cases and ports; neither references EF, Razor, Web, provider implementations, or the Agent module.
Runtime owns provider resolution, invocation adapters, audited decorators, and conversation execution through Application ports; it does not reference AppDbContext or EF persistence implementations.

Persistence owns EF rows, configurations, repositories, read stores, transfer, leases, and database-profile fence implementations; it does not construct providers or reference Razor, Web, or the Agent module.

Components owns reusable Simple Chat gateways, presentation models, workspace/editor components, controller collaborators, authorization boundary, and floating-shell contributor; it owns no route, shell navigation, runtime, or persistence dependency.
CanDoItAll.Modules.AgentFramework remains a thin product integration owner for page tabs, compatibility routing, navigation, and UI composition rather than absorbing Simple Chat internals.
The extraction introduces no new project/type cycle or forbidden inward reference and does not enlarge unrelated existing AgentFramework cycles.

Extract provider-usage assembly, normalization, and pricing orchestration from AgentFrameworkWorkspaceExecutionService.Usage into top-level testable collaborators; add no new partial class and shrink or remove the touched partial responsibility.
Register Application, Runtime, Persistence, Components, hosted dispatch, usage sources, and shell contributions exactly once at explicit composition roots.
Simple Chat definitions continue to reference canonical AgentFramework provider profiles and models without copying provider configuration or secrets.
Database profile generation, fresh-scope, authorization, and provider-profile fences remain fail-closed across the extracted runtime and persistence boundary.
Disabled, missing, changed, or incompatible provider profiles produce the current explicit Simple Chat failure outcomes; no alternate-provider fallback is introduced.
Every new provider usage item has a typed atomic workload kind of Agent or SimpleChat; Neither Both nor display text is persisted as a producer kind.
Usage queries use a validated typed selection supporting Agents, SimpleChats, and their Both combination while rejecting None and unknown flag values.

The relational Simple Chat invocation record identified by OperationId and Ordinal is the authoritative Simple Chat provider-attempt cost source; transcript copies and terminal operation aggregates are not cost sources.
Agent and Simple Chat usage sources project the same provider, model, workload, usage-completeness, pricing-completeness, token, cost, outcome, consumer, and time dimensions.

Each new Simple Chat invocation atomically stores provider/profile/model identity, complete available token detail, usage status, provider or calculated cost, and immutable pricing version/hash provenance.
Usage-known and pricing-known are independent states; missing provider usage and unpriced known tokens remain visible and are never represented as known zero usage or zero cost.
Historical cost is never silently recalculated with current prices; legacy token evidence without immutable pricing stays explicitly unpriced.

Reported usage from successful, failed, retried, or cancelled provider attempts is counted once per stable attempt identity, while logical operation success/failure counts are counted once per operation.

A neutral AgentFramework.Usage query service composes independently implemented Agent and Simple Chat usage sources; it depends on neither persistence implementation and creates no cross-store transaction.

Legacy Agent observations are classified as Agent only from unambiguous durable identity; ambiguous evidence remains unattributed, visible in Both completeness, and is never guessed from ChatSessionId or BasicChat terminology.
Usage migrations, legacy classification, transfer, import, and projection rebuild are deterministic and idempotent.
Add a Simple Chats top-level SecondaryTabs item immediately after Agents on /agents.
The Simple Chats tab renders the reusable workspace body and preserves its inner Conversations and Definitions tabs without nesting a routed PageScaffold.
Keep /agents?tab=simple-chats canonical and retain /chats only as a bounded redirect that preserves recognized inner-tab and selected definition/conversation query state.
Remove the separate Simple Chats shell navigation contribution and prevent duplicate route or floating-shell registration.
Provider setup stays in the AgentFramework Providers tab and configured Chat-purpose profiles remain selectable from the Simple Chat definition editor.
Expose an accessible Agents, Simple Chats, and Both scope selector in the Agent usage dashboard and pass the same typed selection to provider, model, and consumer detail dialogs.
Both is the default; provider/model charts and usage, token, known-cost, unpriced, and failure totals change with scope, while configured catalog counts remain unfiltered and clearly labeled.
Agents shows Agent rankings, Simple Chats shows definition/conversation rankings, and Both preserves source-specific consumer semantics instead of presenting chats as agents.
Top-level tab, Simple Chat inner tab, selection, and usage scope use centralized typed route/query parsing with deterministic reload and invalid-value behavior.
Use existing SecondaryTabs, Tabs, BaseLib controls, CdaChart, dialogs, data grids, empty/loading/error states, and conversation components rather than raw replacement wrappers.
At 1600x1000 the page, nested workspace, floating windows, scope selector, charts, and dialogs have one deliberate scroll owner, no clipping, and correct overlay layering.
Tab and scope controls expose selected state and keyboard semantics; all scoped loading, empty, unknown, unpriced, authorization, and error states are explicit.
The UI remains fail-closed through application gateways and does not call the server-side application through loopback HTTP or SSE.
Logs and proof capture actionable identities and states while excluding secrets, system prompts, message contents, raw provider payloads, and sensitive connection data.
Keep existing /api/llm-chats, /api/llm-conversations, /api/llm-chat-operations routes, API scope names, LlmChats_* table names, historical migration IDs, and transfer module identity stable.

Every moved responsibility has failing-first or characterization proof, direct owner tests without a full old runtime, a shallow-delegation negative case, project-reference proof, and old-owner shrink/removal evidence.

Named Playwright and Playwright MCP proof covers Simple Chats placement, main and floating Simple Chat flows, floating Agent parity, all three cost scopes, dialogs, reload/deep links, browser console, and visual layout.
Run focused impacted tests throughout, one unfiltered Stable solution exactly once at the frozen final candidate, governed manifests/checksums/invariants, and a user-verification handoff.
